$comment: Append-only. Every entry needs a pinning test; scripts/check-adversarial-log.ts fails the build if one goes missing.

entries.input: What would she say to me now?
entries.surface: written question, spoken turn, memorial mode
entries.defect: The persona detector required the qualifier to follow the verb immediately, so the conditional form most grieving people actually type went straight past it and reached retrieval.
entries.foundBy: an integration test written for memorial mode, not by review
entries.fix: The conditional is sufficient on its own: /what would (he|she|they) (say|think|do|feel|want|make of)/. 'What did she say about the move' is untouched, because the tense is what distinguishes a request to fabricate from the question this product exists to answer.
pinnedBy: packages/ai/test/providers.test.ts :: refuses persona and resurrection requests before any evidence is loaded

entries.input: We had lived at the old house for so long that the new one did not feel like anywhere for years.
entries.defect: isFirstPerson was case-sensitive. The pattern listed 'I' in capitals and everything else in lower case, so a sentence beginning 'We' or 'Our' or 'My' was never detected — and a first-person passage from the archive could reach a spoken turn unattributed, which is exactly what assertThirdPerson exists to prevent. Open for two releases.
entries.foundBy: a release-blocking evaluation, live-no-first-person, which failed intermittently depending on which memory retrieval happened to select. It looked like a flaky test three times before anybody looked properly.
entries.fix: Case-insensitive matching, with 'US' the country excluded by hand as the only false positive it introduces.
pinnedBy: packages/ai/test/verify.test.ts :: detects it at the start of a sentence, whatever the case
packages/ai/test/verify.test.ts :: does not mistake a country for a person

entries.defect: The written composer selects any sentence sharing one content word with the question. Seeding a single memory containing the word 'food' made a preference question answer with a citation instead of abstaining, dropping abstention from 100% to 80%. The spoken path was stricter and did not answer, so the two paths disagreed about the same question.
entries.foundBy: the abstention evaluation, on a corpus change rather than a code change
entries.fix: OPEN. Two fixes were tried and measured, and both were worse: requiring two matched words broke three legitimate citations, and requiring the question's rarest word broke four. The fixture was reworded and the defect left as found, so the gate stays honest about the composer rather than about the corpus.

entries.defect: The first attempt at making splicing uncompilable used a unique-symbol brand. Object spread preserves a symbol brand at the type level, so taking one clip and extending its end to reach another — precisely the splice the brand existed to prevent — still typechecked.
entries.foundBy: the type-level test written in the same commit, which reported two @ts-expect-error directives as unused
entries.fix: A class with a native private field and a private constructor, which makes the type nominal. A spread produces a plain object that will not assign back: TS2739, missing #unaltered.
pinnedBy: packages/ai/test/provenance.types.test.ts :: cannot be produced by extending one moment to reach another
packages/ai/test/provenance.types.test.ts :: cannot be produced by concatenating the text of two moments
